# HS-3G: a sub-250 g 3-inch GPS quad (drone proving ground)

**Status: design package only. Nothing here has been bought, cut, built, weighed, powered or flown.** Every number below is regenerated by `build_hs3g_package.py` from the cited inputs in `inputs/`, the CadQuery solids it builds, and the files that PRs #276 and #291 committed. `tests/test_drone_proving_ground.py` regenerates the package and fails if this README drifts.

```bash
PYTHONPATH=src <python with cadquery> examples/drone_proving_ground/build_hs3g_package.py          # rewrite README, results, CAD
PYTHONPATH=src <python with cadquery> examples/drone_proving_ground/build_hs3g_package.py --check  # fail on drift
```

## 1. What the existing drone PRs already proved

The 2026-11-13 independent audit of the four drone PRs found the arithmetic almost entirely right and the errors in what the numbers stand for. Taken at its word, and re-derived where this package depends on it:

| PR | Proved | Did not prove |
|---|---|---|
| #230 System Example 001 (Crazyflie 2.1+ + sensor deck) | Crazyflie specs match Bitcraze's page; deck mass/current arithmetic; pinned firmware and KiCad template | Deck mass and current are illustrative, not measured. The PR's three-gate run was recorded as "queued"; it finished as **failure** (fixed by #231). The Crazyflow run steps **one control period**: it shows the library runs, not dynamics. |
| #231 Kbuild and headless-sim fixes | All three gates pass on its head (run 41110275012): an inert app links into the pinned firmware; the simulator runs headless | No physical quantity at all |
| #276 whoop65 CAD, fabrication pack, PyBullet flight | A closed 2-manifold frame with the intended interfaces (26 x 26 FC, 3 x M1.4 on 6.6 mm, 31 mm props); its mass estimate (9.04 g PETG) is right; fabrication pack hashes match | The PyBullet flight is upstream's 27 g **Crazyflie** model, not the whoop. Printability, fit, strength, thrust: unmeasured. All-up mass was never stated. |
| #291 build-vs-buy priced BOM | The price tool and its sums | Three "cheapest" lines were the wrong item (rotor bell, canopy, O4/3-in-1 board); corrected build minimum NT$5,484, not NT$4,036 |

**None of it is physical evidence of a drone.** The audit's recommendation, followed here, is to move the first proving ground from the 65 mm whoop to a sub-250 g 3-inch quad with GPS return-to-home, keep the whoop only as an optional print-and-fit exercise, and make a 5-inch the second proving ground.

## 2. What this package adds

- **A requirements decision** (sub-250 g 3-inch, section 4) with the numbers that justify it.
- **Five strategies compared with sources** (section 5): buy a GPS BNF, a PX4/Pixhawk kit, the Crazyflie reference, the corrected whoop build, and a custom 3-inch.
- **A chosen architecture with exact part identities and prices** (section 6), each tied to a URL and a source class.
- **Quantitative checks computed in code** (section 7): all-up mass with density sensitivity, thrust-to-weight from the maker's thrust table, hover power, current and flight time, battery C-rating, ESC current margin, arm stiffness and first bending mode against the rotor-frequency band, prop clearances and centre of gravity.
- **A parametric CadQuery frame** exported to STEP, STL and a DXF cut profile, with checks read back off the solid and the mesh (section 8).
- **The audit's corrections recomputed from the committed PR files** (section 3), not copied.
- **A list of what only physical testing can prove** (section 9).

## 4. Requirements: sub-250 g 3-inch, decided

| Requirement | Value | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Take-off mass | < 250 g with a 15 g design margin | EU class C0 is "MTOM less than 250 g including payload"; the FAA's recreational registration exception is "less than 250 grams" (sources below). Below the line, registration and prop-energy exposure stay low for a first physical loop. |
| Useful function a commodity whoop lacks | GPS position hold and return-to-home, a payload allowance, outdoor flight | The audit's point that "useful" fails at 65 mm (payload 0, indoor, a few minutes) |
| Thrust-to-weight | >= 3 at the throttle limit, also at 249 g | Wind margin for GPS modes and gusts |
| Hover endurance | Report it | Not a hard gate: it is an extrapolation until measured |
| Open firmware with GPS failsafe | INAV or ArduPilot target for the exact FC | RTH must be configurable and inspectable |
| Parts | Commodity, individually replaceable, each with a URL | "From obtainable parts" |

**Why not 5-inch first.** A 5-inch has the best parts availability and payload, but it is usually well over the 250 g line, its props cause serious injury, and early tests need an outdoor field. With no physical test yet on any HS aircraft, the first physical loop should be the safer one. The method here (sizing, stack, UART map, GPS failsafe, frame) carries over unchanged; only the inputs change.

Regulation sources: <https://www.easa.europa.eu/en/document-library/easy-access-rules/online-publications/easy-access-rules-unmanned-aircraft-systems?page=19> (regulator_search); <https://www.faa.gov/air_traffic/publications/aim_html/chap11_section_2.html> (regulator_search). Taiwan's CAA threshold should be confirmed on drone.caa.gov.tw by the owner (section 10).

## 5. Strategies compared

Radio, goggles and charger are needed by every option and are left out of every row. Prices are as listed on the access date in the seller's currency; nothing was ordered.

| Strategy | Identity | Price | Take-off mass | Flight time | Payload | Firmware |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Buy a sub-250 g GPS micro long-range BNF | Flywoo Explorer LR 4 V2.2 analog BNF with GPS (4-inch, 1404 2750KV, GOKU stack) | US$278.49; US$239.99 same item shown sold out on a collection page | 229 g (see note) | not stated | not stated | Betaflight/INAV-capable F4 stack (vendor configuration) |
| PX4/Pixhawk open development kit | Holybro PX4 Development Kit X500 v2 (Pixhawk 6C, M10 GPS, 915 MHz telemetry) | US$609.00 | 610 g (see note) | 18 min | 1500 g | PX4 (shipped), ArduPilot |
| Closed nano reference (existing System Example 001) | Bitcraze Crazyflie 2.1+ with an HS sensor deck (PR #230/#231) | US$240.00 (audit estimate) | 29 g | 7 min | 15 g | Crazyflie firmware (open source) |
| 65 mm printed whoop build (PR #276 / #291) | HS65 printed frame + BETAFPV Matrix 1S 5-in-1 + 0702 motors + Gemfan 1210-2 | NT$5,484 (corrected minimum) | 38.0 g (computed) | unmeasured | 0 g | Betaflight |
| Custom sub-250 g 3-inch GPS quad (this package) | HS-3G: HS-generated carbon frame + SpeedyBee F405 Mini stack + 4x F1404 3800KV + HQ T3x3x3 + M10Q-5883 + 4S 650 mAh, INAV or ArduPilot | US$336.98 (section 6) | 203.9 g (computed) | 8.0 min hover (extrapolated) | 30.4 g allowance | INAV (SPEEDYBEEF405MINI) or ArduPilot (SpeedyBeeF405Mini) |

- **Buy a sub-250 g GPS micro long-range BNF.** For: Cheapest path to a flying GPS sub-250 g aircraft; tuned by the maker; no fabrication risk. Against: No HS design content: the integration loop the mission asks for (sizing, stack, UART map, frame, payload mount) is done by the vendor. Payload mounting is whatever the frame allows.
  Mass note: Flywoo lists about 229 g takeoff for the O4 Wide version with its 4S 750 mAh pack; the analog V2.2 figure was not reached.
  Sources: <https://www.racedayquads.com/products/flywoo-bnf-explorer-lr-4-v2-2-4-4s-analog-choose-receiver-gps> (retailer_search); <https://flywoo.net/products/explorer-lr4-o4-wide> (maker_search)
- **PX4/Pixhawk open development kit.** For: Best autonomy stack and the largest payload of any option; mature open firmware and documentation. Against: Over the 250 g line before the battery is fitted (ratio computed below), so registration and larger-prop hazards apply; costs more than any other option; needs an outdoor field for every test.
  Mass note: Kit weight without battery per Holybro; a 4S 3000-5000 mAh pack adds several hundred grams.
  Sources: <https://holybro.com/products/px4-development-kit-x500-v2> (maker_page)
- **Closed nano reference (existing System Example 001).** For: Excellent firmware and sensing testbed; already integrated in this repository. Against: A finished product, indoor-only, with the smallest payload and endurance in the table. It does not answer 'from obtainable parts'.
  Price note: Not on the Bitcraze product page; the 2026-11-13 audit gives 'about US$240 bare' from store and RobotShop listings.
  Sources: <https://www.bitcraze.io/products/crazyflie-2-1-plus/> (maker_page)
- **65 mm printed whoop build (PR #276 / #291).** For: Cheapest first print-and-fit loop; indoor-safe. Against: Corrected build minimum is above the cheapest BNF; FDM frame is heavier than the PP and printed frames it replaces; payload is zero; governing thrust number unpublished.
  Sources: `examples/arbitrage_lab/build_vs_buy/evidence/drone_whoop65_20261106.json` (repo); `examples/drone_lab/fabrication/20261105/GEOMETRY_AUDIT.json` (repo)
- **Custom sub-250 g 3-inch GPS quad (this package).** For: Every engineering variable is HS's to set and check; open firmware with GPS return-to-home; payload mass and mount are designed in; parts are commodity and individually replaceable; the method carries to a 5-inch. Against: Costs more than the GPS BNF (section 5 decision); nothing about it has been built, weighed or flown.
  Sources: `inputs/parts.json` (repo)

**Decision: build the custom 3-inch, knowing it does not win on price.** The parts total US$336.98 against US$278.49 for the GPS BNF (US$58.49 more; US$96.99 more than its sold-out US$239.99 price). US$65.00 of the build total is assumption or lower bound. The reason to build is the mission, not the money: the BNF does the integration loop for you, and the proving ground exists to show HS doing it (sizing, current budget, UART map, frame, payload mount, failsafe configuration) on an aircraft whose parts can each be checked and replaced. If the owner only wants a GPS sub-250 g aircraft, buy the BNF (section 10).

The PX4 kit is the right tool for autonomy work but is not a sub-250 g aircraft: 610 g without a battery is 2.44x the 250 g line, at 1.81x the HS-3G parts cost. The Crazyflie is a testbed, not a build; and the corrected whoop costs more than a BNF while weighing more than the frame it replaces.

## 6. Chosen architecture: HS-3G

X quad, 135 mm motor-to-motor diagonal, 76.2 mm (3-inch) props, 4S. SpeedyBee F405 Mini BLS 35A 20x20 stack (F405 Mini FC, ICM42688P, DPS310 baro, 16 MB flash; BLS 35A Mini V2 ESC). Firmware: INAV (`SPEEDYBEEF405MINI`) first, ArduPilot (`SpeedyBeeF405Mini`) as the alternative; both targets exist upstream at the pinned commits in `inputs/parts.json`. The FC has 6 hardware UARTs, 1 of them routed to Bluetooth, leaving 5 for 3 needs (receiver (CRSF), GNSS, VTX SmartAudio/Tramp) and 2 spare for a payload or telemetry link. The battery hangs under the bottom plate on a strap, so nothing heavy is in the prop plane; the GNSS/compass sits on the top plate 30 mm above the bottom plate, away from ESC current.

## 7. Quantitative checks

### 7.1 All-up mass

AUW **203.87 g** (116.87 g dry + 87 g pack). The carbon frame is 23.76 g from the CadQuery volume (13.121 + 2.208 cm³) at 1.55 g/cm³; across the assumed 1.5-1.6 g/cm³ range the AUW is 203.10-204.63 g. Standoffs are 1.411 g each (502.3 mm³ of 7075 at 2.81 g/cm³). Under the 250 g line with the 15 g margin, **30.4 g is left for a payload** (computed at the heavy end of the density range).

### 7.2 Thrust-to-weight

From the maker's bench table for the F1404 3800KV on HQ 3x3x3 at about 15.8 V (https://www.ligpower.com/product/f1404-kv3800-fpv-motor.html): 1,204.1 g total at 100 % throttle, **T/W 5.91**. With the throttle limit from 7.4 (70 %), 1,036.6 g, **T/W 5.08**. At a 249 g take-off mass (the whole payload allowance used and more) the limited T/W is 4.16. All three clear the 3 requirement. Bench voltage is above a sagging 4S pack, so these are upper bounds.

### 7.3 Hover power, current and flight time

Hover needs 50.97 g per motor, far below the table's lowest row (187.04 g at 50 %), so hover is an extrapolation. A log-log fit over the 50-70 % rows gives P ∝ T^1.835 and 8.6 W/motor; momentum-theory scaling (P ∝ T^1.5) from the 50 % row gives 13.43 W/motor. The package uses the more pessimistic **13.43 W/motor**. Ideal induced power is 3.343 W/motor (air density 1.225 kg/m³), an overall hover efficiency of 0.249, which is in the plausible range for a small motor at low load. Estimated hover rpm 10,319 (rpm ∝ √T).

With 4 W of avionics at 14.8 V nominal, hover draws **3.9 A** (6.0C). Using 80% of 650 mAh, **hover time is about 8.0 min** (6.0 min at 249 g). With the GF3016 prop instead, 8.6 min; its blade count is not stated on the maker table, so it is not the primary choice. Forward flight, wind and pack sag change this; only a logged flight measures it.

### 7.4 Battery C-rating and ESC current margin

Full throttle draws 77.9 A (4 x 19.4 A + avionics). The pack's rated 70C continuous is 45.5 A and 140C burst is 91.0 A. **Sustained full throttle exceeds the continuous rating** (burst covers it). The design therefore limits throttle to about **70 %** of the bench ESC command (INAV `throttle_scale`, ArduPilot `MOT_SPIN_MAX`; how a setting maps to ESC command is itself a bench check), which draws 44.2 A, inside the continuous rating, and still gives T/W 5.08. Hobby C-ratings are optimistic; a logged current trace on the first pack decides whether the limit can rise.

The ESC is rated 35 A continuous per motor (45 A for 5 s). The worst table row is 19.4 A per motor, a **1.8x margin**; the motor's own 60 s peak rating is 19 A. Prop tip speed at full throttle is 111.3 m/s (Mach 0.324).

### 7.5 Arm stiffness and first bending mode

Each arm is a 12 x 3 mm carbon cantilever with a free length of 44.87 mm (motor centre to where the arm axis leaves the body) and a 11.64 g tip mass (motor, prop, screws). With E = 55.2 GPa: stiffness 49.49 N/mm, tip deflection 0.0597 mm and root stress 7.36 MPa at full thrust; **first out-of-plane bending mode about 320 Hz**. With the pessimistic E = 40 GPa it is 272 Hz.

Rotor frequency runs from about 172 Hz at hover to 465 Hz at full throttle, so the arm mode **is inside the operating band** (crossed near 19,209 rpm, or 16,351 rpm at low E). Hover blade-pass is about 516 Hz. That is normal for 3-inch frames and is what RPM-based notch filtering (INAV/ArduPilot with bidirectional DShot) is for; static deflection and stress are negligible. Crash loads, not flight loads, size these arms, and only a crash or drop test measures them.

### 7.6 Prop clearance and centre of gravity

The prop disc spans z = 19.6-25.6 mm (motor height plus an assumed 6 mm hub). Adjacent prop tips are **19.26 mm** apart (minimum 10). Parts that reach the prop plane and their radial clearance to the nearest prop tip: standoff 3.59 mm, vtx 15.26 mm (minimum 3 mm). No part above the prop plane overlaps a prop disc in plan; the underslung battery sits 19.6 mm below the prop plane.

Placing every part at its layout position, the battery centre must sit **1.05 mm** forward of the frame centre for a zero x offset; the 58 mm pack still spans both strap slots. The CG is then 18.05 mm below the prop plane (z = 1.55 mm), with 203.86 g accounted for.

## 8. Frame CAD

`hs3g_frame.py` builds two plates in CadQuery: a 3 mm unibody bottom plate (60 x 32 mm body, 12 mm arms, 19 mm motor pads, 20 x 20 M3 stack holes, two strap slots) and a 1.5 mm top plate on four M3 x 30 mm standoffs. Each motor pad carries **both** a 9 mm and a 12 mm M2 bolt circle, because the F1404 drawing could not be read and listings disagree. `build_hs3g_package.py` exports STEP, binary STL and a DXF cut profile per plate into `generated/`.

Checks, all read back off the generated solid or mesh rather than the parameters:

| Check | Bottom plate | Top plate |
|---|---|---|
| Valid single solid (OCC) | True | True |
| STL triangles | 25,540 | 2,556 |
| Watertight: every edge shared by exactly 2 triangles, consistently oriented | True (0 bad edges) | True (0 bad edges) |
| Mesh volume vs CAD volume | 13,119.9 vs 13,120.7 mm³ (-0.006 %) | 2,208.2 vs 2,208.2 mm³ (0.0 %) |
| Bounding box (mm) | 114.457 x 114.457 x 3 | 56 x 27 x 1.5 |
| Repo reader `drone_product_delivery.source_binary_stl_info` | 25,540 triangles, 114.457 x 114.457 x 3 | 2,556 triangles |
| Mass at 1.55 g/cm³ | 20.34 g | 3.42 g |

Motor spacing measured from the four 5.5 mm centre holes: diagonals 135, 135 mm (target 135), adjacent 95.459 mm. M2 bolt holes found by bolt-circle diameter: 12 mm x 16, 9 mm x 16.

The CAD is evidence of geometry only: it says nothing about how a cutter handles 3 mm carbon, edge delamination, hole tolerance, or crash strength.

## 9. What only physical testing can prove

Each item names the test that would settle it. Until then the corresponding number above is a prediction.

1. **Real masses.** Weigh every part and the cut plates (predicted frame 23.76 g, AUW 203.87 g). Bench scale.
2. **Motor bolt pattern and fit.** Caliper the F1404 base (9 vs 12 mm PCD); test-fit motors, stack and standoffs on the cut plate.
3. **Hover thrust and power at 50.97 g/motor.** Thrust stand below the 50 % throttle row where the maker table starts; this replaces the extrapolation in 7.3.
4. **Pack current and sag.** Logged current at the 70 % limit and in punch-outs; confirms or moves the throttle limit (7.4).
5. **Flight time.** Hover and cruise on a logged pack to the 80% capacity line (predicted 8.0 min hover).
6. **Frame resonance.** Blackbox gyro spectrum across the throttle range; look for the predicted arm mode near 272-320 Hz and set notch filters.
7. **Motor and ESC temperature** after a hard pack (the maker's bench temperatures are recorded in `inputs/motor_f1404_3800kv_thrust.json`).
8. **Compass interference.** Compass calibration and a current-vs-heading log with motors running.
9. **GPS failsafe and return-to-home.** Props-off failsafe checks first, then a supervised RTH test in an open field; legal flying site required.
10. **Prop clearance under load.** Video at full throttle; blade flex and the assumed hub height are not modelled.
11. **Crash survival.** Drop and crash tests of the arms and pads; flight-load stress here is negligible, so crashes decide arm size.
12. **Radio and video range** with the chosen antennas and mounting.

## 10. Decisions for the owner

1. **Build or buy.** Building costs US$58.49 more than the GPS BNF on today's listings. Build only if the proving-ground value (section 5) is the point.
2. **Frame cutting.** The 3 mm bottom plate is not on SendCutSend's standard carbon list; choose a cutter and get a real quote for the DXFs in `generated/`.
3. **INAV or ArduPilot.** INAV is the recommended first firmware (simpler multirotor GPS setup on this class); ArduPilot is supported by the same FC.
4. **Whoop source files.** The audit's corrections are recomputed here but not written into `examples/drone_lab/` or `examples/arbitrage_lab/build_vs_buy/`, because those are dated records with committed hashes. Decide whether to correct them in place.
5. **Taiwan registration threshold.** Confirm on drone.caa.gov.tw that 250 g is the line that applies.
6. **Mission document.** `docs/HARDWARE_SPLICER_MISSION_FREEZE.md` is still not on main.
7. **Not applied from the audit:** 291-28 (cyberdeck comparator) and the p25/median recomputation in 291-3/291-7, which needs #291's price tool to keep every listing.

## 11. Files

| File | Role |
|---|---|
| `inputs/parts.json` | Part identities, masses, prices, source URLs and classes; materials; named assumptions |
| `inputs/motor_f1404_3800kv_thrust.json` | The maker's F1404 3800KV thrust table, transcribed |
| `inputs/strategies.json` | Strategy comparison inputs and sources |
| `hs3g_frame.py` | Parametric CadQuery frame, measurement and export |
| `hs3g_design.py` | Mass, CG, clearance, propulsion, arm and mesh checks |
| `hs3g_audit.py` | Audit corrections recomputed from the #276/#291 files |
| `build_hs3g_package.py` | Regenerates everything; `--check` fails on drift |
| `hs3g_readme.py` | Renders this README from `generated/results.json` |
| `generated/` | `results.json`, STEP, STL and DXF for both plates |
| `tests/test_drone_proving_ground.py` | Regenerates into a temp dir and checks CAD, numbers and README |
